bugs.name: Relative links and image paths on a page with a slash in its title resolve against the wiki root
bugs.summary: Both are rewritten to the wrong place. The saved page's HTML is — the page's own directory agent3imgdir/ is dropped, so the browser asks for the wiki root file pic.png instead of agent3imgdir/pic.png. The parent reference becomes — not a raw path at all (a wiki page address), so no file can ever load. Both images render as broken-image icons (alt text shown). On a page at the wiki root the same syntax works: ![x](Home.md) becomes /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/raw/Home.md, which serves the file. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/agent3imgdir/sub)
bugs.expected: Relative image paths resolve against the page's own location in the wiki repository: ![sibling](pic.png) on the page agent3imgdir/sub must request /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/raw/agent3imgdir/pic.png, and ![parent](../up.png) must request /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/raw/up.png, so an image stored next to the page loads.
bugs.actual: Both are rewritten to the wrong place. The saved page's HTML is — the page's own directory agent3imgdir/ is dropped, so the browser asks for the wiki root file pic.png instead of agent3imgdir/pic.png. The parent reference becomes — not a raw path at all (a wiki page address), so no file can ever load. Both images render as broken-image icons (alt text shown). On a page at the wiki root the same syntax works: ![x](Home.md) becomes /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/raw/Home.md, which serves the file.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki?action=_new
Enter the page title agent3imgdir/sub (a page in a wiki subdirectory) and the content: "Sibling image: ![sibling](pic.png)" newline "Parent image: ![parent](../up.png)"
Click Save Page → the page opens at /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/agent3imgdir%2Fsub with both images shown as broken images

Compare with a page at the wiki root: create agent3imgtest with "![plain](Home.md)" — its img src is /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/raw/Home.md, which serves the file, while the subdirectory page's src values are /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/raw/pic.png and /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/up.png
bugs.reason: Gitea 1.24 wikis have no sub-directories: a slash in a title is stored as %2F in one root-level file, and the link resolver states the path options are unused "because Wiki doesn't support sub-path". Resolving every relative link from the wiki root is therefore the designed behaviour.

bugs.actual: The table overflows the wiki content card: at rest the fifth column is clipped at the viewport edge ('Colur five'), and sideways scrolling moves the WHOLE document (the card's left border and the first column's text 'umn one' are cut off on the left, the header and footer shift with it). reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and set the browser viewport to 390x844.
Open https://5503-ixlrdcr4kwxgn019fmdah.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/wiki?action=_new

bugs.name: A wiki address containing %00 returns a blank 400 page
bugs.summary: The server answers HTTP 400 with an empty body: the browser shows a completely blank white page — no site header, no error message, no link back to the wiki or anywhere else. Navigating away with the browser's Back button is the only way out. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/agent5-alpha%00.-)
bugs.expected: A clean error state: an error page saying the page address is not valid (404/400 state) with the usual Gitea header and a way back to the wiki, like other wrong wiki addresses.
bugs.actual: The server answers HTTP 400 with an empty body: the browser shows a completely blank white page — no site header, no error message, no link back to the wiki or anywhere else. Navigating away with the browser's Back button is the only way out.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1
Open the address https://5503-ixlrdcr4kwxgn019fmdah.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/agent5-alpha%00.- (a wiki page address with an encoded NUL character %00 in the page name)
The response is HTTP 400 and the tab is a blank white page
bugs.reason: An encoded NUL byte is malformed input that no link in the app produces, and 400 Bad Request is the correct answer to it. The evidence does not show whether Gitea or the sandbox proxy sent the empty body, and no handler in the wiki router returns a 400.

bugs.name: A wiki page re-created under a deleted page's name shows the old page's revisions
bugs.summary: The new page's header badge and the revision history page say "5" / "5 Commits", listing the whole life of the deleted page: "Add recyc-14" (the original), "Update recyc-14", "Update recyc-14", "Delete page \"recyc-14.-\"" and the new "Add recyc-14". The re-created page contains only the new content, yet it inherits the deleted page's revisions — including the deletion commit — and the count is 5 for a page that was just created, directly contradicting the delete dialog's "cannot be undone". (on /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/recyc-14.-?action=_revision)
bugs.expected: A page created again under a name whose earlier page was deleted should start with a fresh history: 1 revision ("Add recyc-14") and one commit, matching the "Deleting the wiki page … cannot be undone" promise — or, if old history is kept deliberately, the deleted page's revisions should not be presented as the new page's own revisions/count.
bugs.actual: The new page's header badge and the revision history page say "5" / "5 Commits", listing the whole life of the deleted page: "Add recyc-14" (the original), "Update recyc-14", "Update recyc-14", "Delete page \"recyc-14.-\"" and the new "Add recyc-14". The re-created page contains only the new content, yet it inherits the deleted page's revisions — including the deletion commit — and the count is 5 for a page that was just created, directly contradicting the delete dialog's "cannot be undone".
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1, open /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki?action=_new, enter the page title "recyc-14", put "Content A for recycle test" in the body and click "Save Page".
Edit the page twice, changing the body to "Content B for recycle test" and then "Content C for recycle test", saving each time (the page now shows the revision badge "3").
On the page click the red "Delete Page" button, then "Yes" in the "Deleting the wiki page "recyc-14" cannot be undone. Continue?" dialog (the app returns to the wiki Home page).
Open /eval/harbor-handbook/wiki?action=_new again, use exactly the same title "recyc-14", put "Content D for recycle test" in the body and click "Save Page".
Look at the revision badge next to the page name and click it to open the revision history.
bugs.reason: Wiki revisions are by design the Git log of the page's file path (FileCommitsCount and CommitsByFileAndRange on pageFilename), so a file re-created at the same path carries the earlier commits, delete commit included. "Cannot be undone" refers to the delete action in the UI, not to erasing Git history.
